name: Panel Workspace
description: Renders deterministic terminal panel layouts, directional, cyclic, positional, and visible focus or swap selection, child-terminal navigation, exact-current-directory Tab creation, directional keyboard movement, proportional equalization, resize, split, drag, and close behavior.

states: Split the active terminal into multiple panels and inspect headers, inactive masks, separators, and menu actions.
Split three Panels into a nested layout, cycle focus forward and backward through canonical leaf order, and inspect both wrap boundaries and terminal-input continuity.
Split three Panels into a nested layout, focus exact canonical positions with Control+Shift+1 through 3, and confirm a missing position falls through without changing focus.
Select a child terminal the Server published, then inspect the return, title, panel options, close, and child-strip presentation.
Focus a primary or child terminal, press Option+Command+Enter, create a Tab in that exact displayed terminal's current directory, and inspect source identity preservation.
Drag a primary panel header across directional targets and inspect reversible projection and cancellation.
Split four Panels into a nested layout, then move the active Panel with Shift plus the directional-focus chord and inspect exact leaf exchange without topology or terminal-identity changes.
Split three Panels along one axis, resize them unevenly, then invoke Equalize Panels and inspect proportional thirds without topology, focus, or terminal-identity changes.
Split the active terminal, press Command+R, then use W, N, T, S, Control-modified steps, and R reset in keyboard resize mode.
Inspect a three-Panel visible focus-selection session, physical labels, inactive targeting surfaces, and the exclusive keyboard scope.
Inspect a three-Panel visible swap-selection session, source exclusion, pointer targets, and source-focus preservation after commit.

useWhen: A Workbench terminal tab needs the reviewed multi-panel model and its complete interaction projection.

Panel identity, directional, cyclic, positional, and visible focus or swap selection, layout, terminal children, exact-current-directory Tab creation, equalization, resize, drag, split, and close must remain coordinated.
avoidWhen: The layout is generic resizable application chrome with no terminal or Workbench panel semantics.
The caller only needs a low-level resizable primitive or one standalone terminal viewport.
invariants: Every tab retains at least one Panel and exactly one focused Panel resolves inside that tab.
Current-directory Tab creation revalidates the exact displayed Presentation and uses only its trusted current CWD without mutating the source terminal.
Cyclic focus follows canonical depth-first Panel-leaf order, wraps only within the active Tab, and delegates the exact target through the existing focus transition.

Positional focus resolves exact one-based positions 1 through 10 in canonical depth-first Panel-leaf order, never clamps a missing target, and delegates the exact target through the existing focus transition.

Visible focus or swap selection captures exact Tab, source focus, maximization, and canonical Panel order; physical labels remain complete beyond one character, and commits delegate only to existing focus or swap Actions.
Dragging changes only reversible projection state until a valid directional drop commits the move.
Directional keyboard movement swaps complete neighboring Panel leaves while preserving split topology, weights, slot identities, terminal identities, and focus on the moved source Panel.
Panel equalization recursively assigns same-axis child weights by descendant Panel units while preserving topology, order, identities, membership, and focus.
Keyboard resize mode captures one exact Tab and Panel, mutates the nearest matching split axis, preserves a visible branch floor, and closes when its target becomes stale.
A Panel's Close ends its primary and every child terminal, whichever one it shows, and closing a Tab's last Panel closes that Tab, as in the TUI.
Closing a terminal that may still run a program, or a Presentation with no terminal, requires localized confirmation before the Server is asked.
A close changes the Panel workspace only when a publication carries the Server's result; nothing waits on a local removal.
Host PTY and process lifecycle remain outside the Panel workspace owner.
